previous_disclosures.summary: Gaming revenue for fiscal year 2023 was $9.07 billion, down 27% from fiscal year 2022, due to excess inventory with channel partners caused by rapid changes in economic conditions. To address this, NVIDIA introduced pricing programs and undershipped GPU supply to lower channel inventory, making meaningful progress in lowering these levels by the end of fiscal year 2023.

In Gaming, NVIDIA announced the Ada Lovelace GPU architecture and introduced products including GeForce RTX 4090, RTX 4080, and RTX 4070 Ti desktop and laptop GPUs, which are featured in over 170 laptop designs. The company also introduced NVIDIA DLSS 3 for over 50 games and applications and brought GeForce RTX 4080-class performance to the GeForce NOW Ultimate membership tier.

comparisons.comparison: Both companies report on their Gaming segment performance for fiscal year 2024, but they exhibit opposite revenue trajectories. NVIDIA reported a 15% increase in Gaming revenue to $10.4 billion, driven by new product launches like the GeForce RTX 4060 and 4070 GPUs and a milestone of 500 AI-powered games. In contrast, AMD reported a 58% decrease in Gaming net revenue to $2.6 billion, primarily attributed to lower semi-custom product revenue.

sentences.text: Gaming revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $10.4 billion, up 15% from fiscal year 2023.
In Gaming, we launched the GeForce RTX 4060 and 4070 GPUs based on the NVIDIA Ada Lovelace architecture.
Gaming net revenue of $2.6 billion in 2024 decreased by 58%, compared to net revenue of $6.2 billion in 2023.
The decrease in net revenue was primarily due to lower semi-custom product revenue.
